authoring_rules: Fourth held-out set (Python + JavaScript/TypeScript), for the go/no-go of the locked purpose-search candidate (harness/experiments/purpose_search/CANDIDATE.md).
Repos chosen because no earlier set, corpus or tuning run used them; four domains (web framework, CLI HTTP client, web framework, schema validation).

Written from each repo's source at the pinned commit before any engine, search or summarizer ran on it. Only a name-only index (candidate pool names) was built, to check that gold and decoys are candidates.
Same rules as sets 1-3: developer phrasing; gold = the function(s) that directly answer; decoys = plausible wrong functions (same stems, the inverse operation, the caller or the helper).
No question contains its gold symbol's name or that name's distinctive verb (set 3's paraphrase rule, e.g. 'work out which application object' not 'find').
Gold and decoys are library code, never test or example files (fastify's and zod's test files are in the candidate pool).

questions.question: How is the signed data a visitor carries between requests written back into a cookie on the reply, and when is that cookie deleted instead?
When a request arrives carrying a signed cookie that was tampered with or is too old, what state does the app start that visitor with?
How does the app choose which registered function deals with a raised exception, checking blueprint-level registrations before app-wide ones and walking up the exception's class hierarchy?
Where do the functions registered to run before every view get called, and how can one of them stop the view from running at all?
How are the hooks that may modify the outgoing reply applied, in which order, and where is the visitor's stored state persisted afterwards?
How does whatever a view returns - a string, a dict, or a tuple carrying a status and headers - get converted into a proper reply object?
How are settings loaded from environment variables that all start with a common name, with double underscores creating nested keys and values parsed as JSON where possible?
When the command-line tool is pointed at a module without naming the application object, how does it work out which object to use, falling back to calling a factory?
When a group of views is mounted under a URL prefix, how are each view's path and endpoint name rewritten before they reach the app?
How is an object serialized into a JSON body for the client, indented in debug mode but compact otherwise?
How long may browsers cache files served from the static folder, and how is that setting converted when it is given as a time span?
What happens when a template is turned into HTML: how is its context filled in, and which notifications fire before and after?
When no HTTP method is typed on the command line, how does the tool decide between a plain read and a request that submits data?
How does an interrupted download carry on where it stopped, asking the server only for the bytes not yet on disk?
How is the server's answer to a partial-content request checked, so that the returned bytes line up exactly with what was already downloaded?
When saving a download, how is a new file name picked so an existing file on disk is never overwritten?
How is the file name suggested in the server's attachment header cleaned up so it cannot point outside the current directory or become a hidden file?
How does the program turn the server's status into its own process exit code, treating 3xx answers differently when redirects are being followed?
How is a request body squeezed with deflate before sending, and when is the smaller version not used because it would not save space?
Which headers does the client send automatically on every request, and how does it choose between JSON and form content types?
Just before a request goes out, how are header values trimmed and turned into bytes, and how are headers the user deliberately emptied kept from being sent?
How does a stored login session work out which cookies are no longer valid because their expiry time or max-age has passed, so they can be dropped?
How is a raw byte count shown as a short readable size such as 1.5 MB in the progress display?
When a response does not declare its character set, how does the tool guess the text encoding before printing the body?
How is the body parser for an incoming content type chosen, matching the media type before any parameters and falling back to pattern-based parsers?
How is a request body read from the socket while enforcing the maximum allowed size, rejecting it up front when the declared length is already too large?
How are JSON request bodies decoded, rejecting empty bodies and protecting the result against prototype-poisoning keys?
When a route throws and nobody registered a custom handler, how is the status chosen and at what log level is the failure recorded?
How does each incoming request get its identifier, either taken from a configured header or produced from an increasing counter?
For the automatically created HEAD routes, how is the body thrown away while still reporting the size the GET answer would have had?
How does the framework decide which forwarding hops in front of the server are believed when working out the client's real address, accepting a hop count, a list of addresses or a custom function?
When the server listens on a host name that resolves to several addresses, such as both IPv4 and IPv6 for localhost, how are the extra addresses bound?
How is the numeric HTTP status of a reply set, rejecting numbers outside 100 to 599?
How does a reply send the client to another URL, keeping a status that was already chosen or otherwise using 302?
In what order are a request's path parameters, body, query string and headers checked against their schemas, and how is the body schema picked by content type?
What does the framework answer when no route matches the method and URL, and is that logged?
When an object is checked against a shape, what happens to keys the shape does not declare: are they kept, rejected with an issue, or silently dropped?
How does a choice between several alternative shapes pick its result, preferring a clean match, then a partly failed one, and otherwise reporting every alternative's problems?
When building a tagged choice of object shapes keyed by one field, how is the lookup table from tag value to shape built, and what makes construction fail?
When two schemas must both hold, how are their two parsed outputs combined into one value, and when are they judged incompatible?
How is a divisibility check done on decimal numbers without floating-point rounding errors?
How is the pattern for ISO date-and-time strings assembled, depending on the allowed fractional-second precision, time-zone offsets and local times?
How is a value that was not provided replaced by a fallback before the inner schema checks it?
When parsing fails, how can a schema substitute a replacement value instead of reporting the failure, while still exposing the original problems to the function that computes the replacement?
How are validation problems grouped into top-level messages and per-field lists keyed by the first segment of their path?
How is an object schema made optional all the way down, including nested objects, arrays and tuples?
For a schema with a pre-step, where is that step run on the raw input before the result is validated?
How is a string checked to be a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address, optionally restricted to one version?
